questions.q: In Import mode, when does Power BI query Snowflake?
options: Only during scheduled refreshes — after that, filters and slicers query Power BI's own in-memory model
On every single filter, slicer, and visual interaction
Only when the report is first published, and never again
Never — Import mode does not require any connection to Snowflake
questions.explain: Import mode copies data into Power BI's model on a schedule; interactions after that are served by Power BI's own engine, not live Snowflake queries.

questions.q: In DirectQuery mode, what happens when a user clicks a slicer?
options: Power BI queries a local cached copy instead of Snowflake
Nothing changes until the next scheduled refresh
The slicer is disabled because DirectQuery doesn't support filtering
Power BI sends a live SQL query straight to Snowflake, translated from that interaction
questions.explain: DirectQuery stores no data — every visual render and interaction triggers a live query against Snowflake.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say DirectQuery's cost risk is worse against Snowflake than against an always-on database server?
options: DirectQuery against Snowflake is free, unlike other databases
Snowflake cannot technically support DirectQuery at all
An always-on server also bills per second, making them identical
Every query runs on a per-second-billed warehouse, and a warehouse resuming from suspension bills a 60-second minimum each time
questions.explain: Snowflake's per-second billing plus the 60-second resume minimum means frequent, bursty DirectQuery traffic can repeatedly trigger that minimum charge throughout the day.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is a practical default for choosing between Import and DirectQuery?
options: Always use DirectQuery because it is always cheaper
The choice has no meaningful cost or freshness tradeoff
Use Import if the data can tolerate being somewhat stale; reserve DirectQuery for genuine near-real-time requirements
Always use Import regardless of freshness requirements
questions.explain: Import turns Snowflake cost into a predictable, schedulable line item; DirectQuery should be reserved for cases where real-time freshness genuinely justifies its less predictable cost.

questions.q: What does this lesson recommend pairing with a DirectQuery-connected report when DirectQuery is the right choice?
options: Switching the warehouse size to the largest available at all times
Removing all RBAC restrictions to speed up queries
A dedicated, appropriately sized reporting warehouse with its own resource monitor
Disabling all resource monitors so queries never get blocked
questions.explain: A dedicated reporting warehouse, sized and monitored separately from ETL/ELT workloads, keeps BI query traffic from starving other workloads or silently dominating the bill.
